1 --- 2 title: forbidden 3 description: API Reference for the forbidden function. 4 version: experimental 5 related: 6 links: 7 - app/api-reference/file-conventions/forbidden 8 - app/api-reference/functions/not-found 9 - app/api-reference/functions/unauthorized 10 - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/authInterrupts 11 --- 12 13 The `forbidden` function throws an error that renders a Next.js 403 page. It's useful for handling authorization errors in your application. You can customize the UI using the [`forbidden.js` file](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/forbidden). 14 15 Invoking `forbidden()` throws a `NEXT_HTTP_ERROR_FALLBACK;403` error and terminates rendering of the route segment where it was thrown. Next.js also injects a `` tag so the page is not indexed. Because it works by throwing, call it in the render path: a component, or a function a component `await`s. A call left in an un-awaited promise throws where nothing catches it, and no forbidden UI renders. 16 17 To start using `forbidden`, enable the experimental [`authInterrupts`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/authInterrupts) configuration option in your `next.config.js` file: 18 19 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 20 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 21 22 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 23 experimental: { 24 authInterrupts: true, 25 }, 26 } 27 28 export default nextConfig 29 ``` 30 31 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 32 module.exports = { 33 experimental: { 34 authInterrupts: true, 35 }, 36 } 37 ``` 38 39 `forbidden` can be invoked in [Server Components](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components), [Server Functions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data), and [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route). 40 41 ```tsx filename="app/admin/page.tsx" switcher 42 import { verifySession } from '@/app/lib/dal' 43 import { forbidden } from 'next/navigation' 44 45 export default async function AdminPage() { 46 const session = await verifySession() 47 48 // Check if the user has the 'admin' role 49 if (session.role !== 'admin') { 50 forbidden() 51 } 52 53 // Render the admin page for authorized users 54 return <> 55 } 56 ``` 57 58 ```jsx filename="app/admin/page.js" switcher 59 import { verifySession } from '@/app/lib/dal' 60 import { forbidden } from 'next/navigation' 61 62 export default async function AdminPage() { 63 const session = await verifySession() 64 65 // Check if the user has the 'admin' role 66 if (session.role !== 'admin') { 67 forbidden() 68 } 69 70 // Render the admin page for authorized users 71 return <> 72 } 73 ``` 74 75 ## Good to know 76 77 - The `forbidden` function cannot be called in the [root layout](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout#root-layout). 78 - You do not need to write `return forbidden()`. It throws (its TypeScript [`never`](https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/2/functions.html#never) return type), so execution stops. A `try/catch` around the call suppresses the interrupt and no forbidden UI renders. Use [`unstable_rethrow`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/unstable_rethrow) to let it through. 79 - A `forbidden()` left in an un-awaited promise throws where nothing catches it, so no forbidden UI renders. In development the server logs `⨯ unhandledRejection: NEXT_HTTP_ERROR_FALLBACK;403`. Always `await` the function that may call it. 80 81 ## Examples 82 83 ### Calling `forbidden()` after streaming has started 84 85 To keep the page's shell and loading UI visible while the session is checked, put the role check in the [Data Access Layer](/docs/app/guides/authentication#creating-a-data-access-layer-dal) function that loads the data, and render it in a component wrapped in [``](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense). The check runs inside the boundary, so the shell streams while the session resolves: 86 87 ```tsx filename="app/projects/page.tsx" switcher highlight={8} 88 import { Suspense } from 'react' 89 import { verifySession } from '@/app/lib/dal' 90 import { forbidden } from 'next/navigation' 91 92 async function getProjects() { 93 const session = await verifySession() 94 if (session?.role !== 'admin') { 95 forbidden() 96 } 97 return db.projects.findMany() 98 } 99 100 async function Projects() { 101 const projects = await getProjects() 102 return ( 103

Because this happens during rendering, the exception propagates to the nearest [`forbidden`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/forbidden) boundary, which renders in place of the streamed-in content, even though the page shell has already been sent. 160 161 Add a `forbidden.tsx` alongside the route to define that UI: 162 163 ```tsx filename="app/projects/forbidden.tsx" switcher 164 export default function Forbidden() { 165 return ( 166

Because the check runs inside the `` boundary, the response has already begun streaming as a `200`, and the status can't change once streaming has started. This is usually fine for a page, where the user sees the `forbidden` UI regardless. To return a real `403` status, the check has to run before the response streams. With [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching), every dynamic route streams a static shell first, so run that check in [`proxy`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/proxy) instead. See [Status codes](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading#status-codes). 186 187 ### Role-based route protection 188 189 You can use `forbidden` to restrict access to certain routes based on user roles. content.text:
Done. Visiting `/admin` as a non-admin now returns a real **HTTP 403** with a styled error page, and none of the admin content leaks into the response (the "Admin Dashboard" string in the HTML is just the root layout's `<title>`).

What I changed:

- **`next.config.ts`** — enabled `experimental.authInterrupts`, which this Next.js version (16.4 canary) requires before `forbidden()` can be used.
- **`app/admin/page.tsx`** — new server component that awaits `getSession()` from the existing mock auth library (`app/lib/auth.ts`) and calls `forbidden()` from `next/navigation` when `session?.role !== 'admin'`. Since `forbidden()` throws, execution stops there; admins fall through to the dashboard, which greets them by name.
- **`app/forbidden.tsx`** — the boundary file that renders when `forbidden()` is thrown. It's a centered "403 — Forbidden" page with a lock icon, a short explanation, and a "Return home" link. Per the docs, this file convention is also what makes Next.js send the 403 status code.

Verified end-to-end: `next build` passes type-checking, and `curl` against `next start` shows `HTTP status: 403` for `/admin` with the forbidden UI in the body. Note the mock `getSession()` currently hardcodes a non-admin user, so everyone gets the 403 until real auth is wired in — flip `role` to `'admin'` in `app/lib/auth.ts` if you want to see the dashboard path.
